look_here_first: LEAVES FIRST, BUT THE SEEDS FINISH THE ID. Euphorbia simulans is a low, largely glabrous desert sandmat with very short opposing ROUND to oval entire leaves (1–3.2 mm long) with near-symmetric bases. The small red-purple cyathial glands are ELLIPTIC and lack the white crescents of E. golondrina; Nathan Taylor's licensed true gland photograph now shows their shape. The smooth green THREE-LOBED capsule is photographed too. The decisive look-alike E. theriaca can look almost identical above ground: true SIMULANS SEEDS are generally 1.5–2 mm with 5–7 WEAK interrupted transverse wrinkles or pits, while THERIACA has smaller seeds with usually 2–4 MUCH DEEPER clear grooves. Both real seed macro photographs and author-stated 0.5mm calibration are now in the genus comparison. Still missing: independently measured same-node 0.5–0.7 mm stipules. FNA records simulans in Brewster, Hudspeth and Presidio; NOT validated as native to Hays or a local crew weed.
photo_note: 8 actual exact-E. simulans public-eligible CC BY-NC photographs: previous five habit/round leaf images with 11 checked arrows, plus three NEW Nathan Taylor micromorphology images with 7 checked arrows showing elliptical reddish appendage-free cyathial glands, smooth three-lobed fruit, and true weakly ridged pale mature seeds with author's HALF-MILLIMETER calibration. E. theriaca deeply ridged seed image kept in genus COMPARISON-MEDIA ONLY, explicitly labeled different taxon. No fabricated stipule closeup or Hays range promotion. Genuine mature E. simulans and E. theriaca seed photos are individually credited by photographer and correctly separated between canonical species and genus comparison.

taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia simulans per POWO and Flora of North America. Not interchangeable with E. polycarpa or E. theriaca; older varietal names can complicate photo searches. FNA reports Texas records from Brewster, Hudspeth and Presidio counties; do not present as a documented Hays plant.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite usually unequal leaves, cyathia rather than ordinary flowers, and 3-lobed capsule that dries and releases seeds.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial; usually slender taproot/rootstock; prostrate to reclining glabrous branches about 5–40 cm, growing in arid desert scrub and rocky or sandy ground.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, ORBICULATE, OVAL or very short oblong, 1–3.2 × 1.5–5 mm; margins entire, rounded base usually SUBSYMMETRIC (unusual for many sandmats), tip rounded or occasionally notched, glabrous. Usually only midvein conspicuous.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct thin awl-shaped (subulate) glabrous scales, 0.5–0.7 mm, at leaf junctions. Distinguish from hairs under a strong lens; existing habit photograph cannot prove individual stipules.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Usually solitary at distal nodes on 0.3–0.7 mm stalks. Cup-like involucre 0.8–1.2 × 0.7–1 mm glabrous; 4 RED TO PURPLE slightly concave ELLIPTIC glands roughly 0.2–0.3 × 0.4–0.5 mm; appendages ABSENT. No white petal-like crescents expected.
morphology_keys.capsules: Broadly ovoid 3-lobed glabrous capsules 1.3–1.8 × 1.5–2 mm; this is compatible with golondrina and cannot resolve both species alone.
morphology_keys.seeds: WHITISH COAT OVER REDDISH-BROWN underneath; narrowly oblong, distinctly 4-angled, 1.5–2 × 1.3–1.8 mm, usually 5–7 FAINT shallow transverse ridges/wrinkles. E. theriaca var. theriaca commonly has smaller seeds with 2–4 PROMINENT transverse ridges. Mature seed macro with calibrated scale needed.
best_field_traits: Very tiny opposite nearly ROUND, entire-margined hairless leaves (1–3.2 mm long)
Subsymmetrical rounded leaf bases unlike strongly oblique leaves of many Chamaesyce
Cyathium at distal node, purple ELLIPTIC glands with NO white appendages
Distinct thin 0.5–0.7 mm glabrous subulate stipules
Mature 1.5–2 mm 4-angled seed with 5–7 weak transverse ridges; essential for close E. theriaca comparison

comparisons.key_distinctions: FIRST leaf shape for golondrina: simulans tiny nearly ROUND entire leaves 1–3.2 mm long versus golondrina generally longer OBONG narrow 5–11.5 mm, with white semilunate gland appendages. Then independently check microscopic elliptic purple glands without appendages in simulans. The closest western species E. theriaca var. theriaca cannot reliably be separated from simulans by ordinary habit photos: simulated 1.5–2 mm mature seeds with 5–7 FAINT transverse wrinkles versus theriaca 0.8–1.2 mm seeds with usually three DEEP cross ridges. E. serpens has fused broad triangular stipules and can root at nodes; E. prostrata has capsule KEEL hairs and strong seed ridges. No genus photo may be relabeled across species.

field_matrix.simulans: Oval to orbiculate 1–3.2 mm long; subsymmetric rounded base
field_matrix.golondrina: Narrow oblong 5–11.5 mm long; asymmetric base
Red-purple subcircular DEEPLY CUPPED with white crescent appendage
field_matrix.theriaca: May resemble simulans; check ripe seed

field_matrix.simulans: Large 1.5–2 mm, 4-angled seeds with 5–7 WEAK shallow transverse ridges or wrinkles
field_matrix.golondrina: 1.3–1.5 mm; faint wrinkles; compare glands and leaf dimensions
field_matrix.theriaca: Typically 0.8–1.2 mm; (2–)3(–4) prominent transverse ridges (var. theriaca), not merely faint surface wrinkling

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tiny rounded leaves → elliptical glands without white crescents → true weakly ridged 1.5–2mm seed
steps: Find reddish low MAT habit and extremely small opposite near-round entire leaf blades; avoid confusing with similarly small seedlings.
Study a real cyathium under 10–20x: E. simulans elliptical RED-PURPLE glands lack petal-like WHITE crescents; compare E. golondrina whose gland pads have white crescents.
Check the real SMOOTH THREE-LOBED green fruit, not the gland-bearing cyathial involucre cup.
To rule out E. theriaca, compare detached seed faces with a half-millimeter ruler: SIMULANS about 1.5–2mm and faint irregular 5–7 ridges, versus THERIACA fewer/deeper (usually 3) furrows.
Get a true same-node 0.5–0.7mm separate threadlike stipule pair for optional close confirmation; not clearly resolved in current images.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The theriaca photograph belongs ONLY to the genus look-alike comparison and is never presented as an E. simulans species photo. Nathan's stated half-millimeter marks are author-calibrated; no independent pixel-derived dimensions claimed. Hays County nativity is not proven.

remaining: Optional in-focus same-node separate subulate stipule pair, source-calibrated 0.5–0.7 mm.
No local Hays County range promotion; FNA Trans-Pecos published distribution only.
